purpose: Canonical contributor, bot, automation, AI-agent, and AI-platform identity registry for repository provenance. Git contribution, declared handoff contribution, operational surfaces, and user-declared tooling are separate evidence classes.

semantics.direct_contribution: Count only Git author/committer identity or an explicit direct-contribution trailer. A tool name in prose, a model catalog, instruction file, branch name, or snapshot path is not direct Git authorship evidence.
semantics.declared_handoff_contribution: An augmentation note that explicitly names an Author/agent records declared participation in that work unit. It is stronger than a surface mention but remains distinct from Git authorship/co-authorship.
semantics.operational_surface: An instruction file, workflow, branch/snapshot name, tracked path, or commit-message reference proves repository interaction/surface only, not authorship of code.
semantics.user_declared: Records a tool the repository owner reports using; it is not attached to individual commits unless direct Git or explicit handoff evidence exists.
semantics.unknown_identity: Unmatched identities remain separate. Heuristics may classify bot-like names but must not alias them to a named service without evidence.
semantics.identity_collision: Generic provider emails, shared service accounts, and GitHub-owned committer identities are not sufficient to map a contribution to a named bot or AI. Prefer unique actor names/IDs or explicit trailers.
semantics.history_rewrites: Squash merges, rebases, cherry-picks, imported snapshots, generated commits, and rewritten commits can collapse or duplicate attribution. The index reports observable Git and handoff evidence and never reconstructs missing authorship by guesswork.
semantics.shared_identity: A human-owned commit created through an AI connector is not automatically AI-authored. Use an explicit trailer or Author/agent handoff declaration to preserve that contribution signal.
semantics.privacy: Generated provenance outputs do not emit raw email addresses. Matching may use Git emails locally; unknown identities receive stable hashed IDs.
